author: reek
body: The second site. A handler clause's resume binder does not escape the clause body -- not into the next clause, not into the handled expression, and not past the `with`.

author: reek
body: The same shape as the try regions, and the same reason it was invisible. The type checker was already right: `infer-handle-clauses` binds the resume name into a fresh env for the clause body and hands the ORIGINAL env to the next clause, so a later read of that word types against whatever was in scope all along. The name resolver was already right too: `resolve-handle-clauses` forks per clause. Only the emitter was not -- `add-local` prepends to a flat list and nothing popped it, so `lookup-local` found the clause's slot for the rest of the function.

author: reek
body: So `resume` below is a chapter-level Text. Inside the clause it is the Integer-taking continuation, which is what the clause means. After the `with`, it is the Text again -- and the emitter used to hand that concatenation the continuation's slot instead.

author: reek
body: What must NOT change: `tick` stays bound after its clause on purpose. The op-name is added AFTER the clause body because the handled expression reads the handler slot through it, and a multi-op handler needs every op still bound when its body runs. The restore therefore goes between the body and the op-name add, not at the end of the clause. `handler-smoke`'s multi-op and nested cases are the ones that fail if that ordering is got wrong.
